fields.name: product_form
fields.rationale: Identifies the product geometry/use class (panels/boards) which is a primary discriminator for wood-based products and important for selection and comparisons.
evidence: "Heradesign acoustic panels are primarily used as acoustic/decorative wall and ceiling panelling"
"Heradesign panels are wood wool panels in accordance with EN 13168"

fields.name: bonding_system
fields.rationale: Type of binder (mineral vs organic) strongly affects performance and environmental behaviour; here the EPD names a magnesite/mineral system.
evidence: "The product is a magnesite bonded wood wool panel."

fields.name: declared_surface_weight_kg_per_m
fields.rationale: Surface (areal) weight is a key material metric for boards/panels used to compare mass per unit area and impacts per functional area; the EPD provides a surface weight value.
evidence: "The declared unit refers to a surface weight of 13.3 kg/m."

fields.name: euroclass_fire_rating
fields.rationale: Fire classification (Euroclass) is commonly used to filter/sort building products by fire performance; the EPD declares Euroclass B.

fields.name: surface_finish_type
fields.rationale: Surface finishing (e.g., dyed/painted, laminated backing) affects aesthetics, durability and end-of-life; the EPD describes dyeing and a back fleece, allowing inference of typical finishes.
evidence: "The production of the acoustic fleece laminated to the back of the Heradesign panels is declared in a separate appendix to the EPD."
inference_basis: Presence of a dyeing plant and RAL colour options implies dyed/painted decorative finishes are offered.
Reference to acoustic fleece laminated to the back implies a laminated backing option is used as a standard accessory.

fields.name: forming_method
fields.rationale: Forming/production method (continuous twin-belt vs. pressing) affects product properties and comparability; text describes a twin-belt continuous forming line allowing an inferred forming method classification.
evidence: "The mixture is scattered onto a steel band and passed through a binding channel... An endless product is produced on leaving the twin belt."
"The raw goods are then cut to the desired length."
inference_basis: Description of scattering onto a steel band and reference to a 'twin belt' implies a continuous twin-belt forming process rather than batch pressing.
